description: Enterprise techniques used by IOControl, ATT&CK software S9046 (v1.0)
name: IOControl (S9046)

techniques.comment: IOCONTROL has used an RC script (`/etc/rc3.d/S93InitSystemd.sh`) to establish persistence on a system across restarts.(Citation: Claroty-IOCONTROL)(Citation: Armis-IOCONTROL)
IOCONTROL has used the AES-256-CBC algorithm to decrypt configuration files associated with the malware.(Citation: Claroty-IOCONTROL) (Citation: Dragos-2026-Year-In-Review)
IOCONTROL has removed the malware binary and associated log file (i.e., `/tmp/iocontrol.log`) from a system upon command.(Citation: Claroty-IOCONTROL)(Citation: Armis-IOCONTROL)
IOCONTROL has removed malware persistence from a system upon command. (Citation: Claroty-IOCONTROL)
IOCONTROL has used the Ultimate Packer for eXecutables (UPX) to pack the malware.(Citation: Claroty-IOCONTROL) (Citation: Dragos-2026-Year-In-Review)

IOCONTROL has used the Advanced Encryption Standard 256-bit Cypher Block Chaining (AES-256-CBC) algorithm to encrypt its configuration files which are used to store information like file paths and IP addresses to connect to. (Citation: Claroty-IOCONTROL) (Citation: Dragos-2026-Year-In-Review)

IOCONTROL has used the `uname -v` and `uname –r` commands to obtain kernel version and release information as well as the `hostname` command to obtain the hostname of the system.(Citation: Claroty-IOCONTROL)(Citation: Armis-IOCONTROL)
IOCONTROL has used the `whoami` command to get the current user on the system.(Citation: Claroty-IOCONTROL)(Citation: Armis-IOCONTROL)
IOCONTROL has used the `date` and `timezone` commands to gather the system date and time information.(Citation: Claroty-IOCONTROL)(Citation: Armis-IOCONTROL)
